﴿And from the evil of the blowers in knots (4) and from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾ [Al-Falaq 4, 5].

﴿The blowers in knots﴾ are the female sorceresses who tie cords and other things, and they blow with an unintelligible recitation in which are the names of devils over these knots, over every knot: they tie, then they blow; they tie, then they blow; they tie, then they blow. Their own wicked selves intend a specific person, and this sorcery takes effect upon the one bewitched.

Allah mentioned the female blowers rather than the male blowers because the one who generally practises this type of sorcery is women, so He said ﴿the blowers in knots﴾. It may also be said that al-naffathat (the blowers) refers to the blowing souls, which would include men and women.

﴿And from the evil of the envier when he envies﴾. The envier is one who dislikes Allah's blessing upon you, so you find him distressed when Allah bestows upon a person wealth, rank, knowledge, or other things, and so he envies him.

Envious people, however, are of two kinds. One kind envies and hates in his heart Allah's blessing upon others, but does not harm the envied person in any way. You find him troubled and grieved by Allah's blessings upon others, but he does not wrong his companion. Evil and calamity come only from the envier when? When he envies, and that is why He said ﴿when he envies﴾.

Among the envy of the envier is the evil eye, which afflicts the one it is cast upon. This man, we ask Allah for well-being, has an aversion to Allah's blessings upon others. When he senses in himself that Allah has bestowed a blessing upon someone, there comes forth from his wicked self a force that we cannot describe, because it is unknown. So he strikes with the evil eye whomever it overpowers. Sometimes the person dies, sometimes he falls ill, and sometimes he goes mad. Even the envier can affect iron, halting its work; perhaps he strikes a car with the evil eye so that it breaks or stops, or perhaps he strikes a water-pump or a plough. The point is that the evil eye is real, and it strikes by the permission of Allah, the Mighty and Majestic.

Allah, the Mighty and Majestic, mentioned the darkness when it settles, the blowers in knots, and the envier when he envies, because all calamity in these three situations is hidden. The night is a veil and a covering: ﴿And by the night when it covers﴾ [Al-Layl 1]. Evil lurks in it and is not known. ﴿The blowers in knots﴾ are likewise: sorcery is hidden and not known. (The envier when he envies.) The evil eye is also hidden: it can come from a person you think is among the dearest of people to you, and you are among the dearest of people to him, yet he strikes you with the evil eye. For this reason Allah singled out these three matters: the darkness when it settles, the blowers in knots, and the envier when he envies. Otherwise they are included in His saying ﴿from the evil of what He created﴾.

If someone asks: what is the way to be freed from these three evils?

We say: the way to freedom is for a person to attach his heart to his Lord, to entrust his affairs to Him, to realise reliance upon Allah, and to use the prescribed litanies (awrad, the fixed devotional recitations) by which he fortifies himself and protects his self from the evil of these people. The matter of sorcerers, envious people, and the like has multiplied among people in recent times only because of their heedlessness of Allah, the weakness of their reliance upon Allah, the scarcity of their use of the prescribed litanies by which they might fortify themselves. Otherwise, we know that the prescribed litanies are an impregnable fortress, stronger than the barrier of Gog and Magog. But unfortunately many people know nothing of these litanies, and whoever knows of them is often heedless, and whoever recites them has a heart that is not present, and all of this is a deficiency. Had people used the litanies as the Shari'ah prescribed, they would have been spared many evils.
